## Data sources

::: {.source-card}
[Primary source]{.source-name}
**Original legislative research** — direct review of primary statutory text, all 50 states

Every entry in this dashboard is based on a dedicated research pass against the actual law: official state code websites, state legislature bill-tracking pages, and reputable full-text legal mirrors (public.law, Justia, FindLaw). Each state's statute citations, covered conditions, covered occupations, service requirements, and effective dates were traced from the primary text itself, not copied from a secondary summary. Every state write-up then went through an independent second review before being added to the dashboard.
:::

::: {.source-card}
[Starting-point reference]{.source-name}
**IAFF Presumptive Health database** — [iaff.org/presumptive-health](https://www.iaff.org/presumptive-health/)

Maintained by the International Association of Fire Fighters, this database was used as an initial lead on where to look in each state — a directory to check, not a source to trust outright. Comparing it against the primary statutory text repeatedly turned up problems: wrong statute citations, outdated effective dates, missing conditions, and mischaracterized benefit types. Where IAFF's page and the actual law disagreed, this dashboard follows the law.
:::

::: {.source-card}
[Cross-check reference]{.source-name}
Neugent, K., & Spidell, B. (2023). *Firefighters and first responders: 2023 update on presumptive workers comp benefits.* National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI).

Covers approximately 38 NCCI-jurisdiction states; data current through November 2022. Used to cross-check IAFF data for covered states during initial extraction.
:::

::: {.source-card}
[Cross-check reference]{.source-name}
Brandt-Rauf, S., Davis, A. L., & Taylor, J. A. (2024). Inventory of state workers' compensation laws in the United States: first responder mental health. *Journal of Public Health Policy*, 45, 562–574.

50-state inventory using the Westlaw legal database; data current through December 2022. Used to supplement IAFF data for mental health / PTSD coverage, which is less consistently documented in other sources.
:::

## Methodology

For each state, a dedicated research pass identified the governing statute(s) directly from primary sources — official state code sites, state legislature bill pages, and full-text legal mirrors — and traced amendment history and effective dates from that text. IAFF's page for the state was checked only as a starting hypothesis about where to look; it was not treated as the final word. Law attributes — condition covered, occupations covered, statute citation, service requirements, post-employment coverage, and restrictions — were then coded into a structured dataset from the verified primary text. Each row represents one state × condition category × occupation combination.

Each completed state write-up went through an independent second review focused on accuracy and completeness before being added to the dashboard. This process found IAFF's page to be wrong, stale, or incomplete for a substantial number of states — citing the wrong statute, using outdated effective dates, omitting conditions or restrictions, or mischaracterizing what type of benefit a law provides — and this dashboard's entries reflect the corrected, source-verified version rather than IAFF's characterization.

Where the primary statutory text itself is ambiguous about whether a provision is historical or currently active, that uncertainty is reflected in the data. A small number of entries are flagged with **\*** in the Notes column where the active status of a statute is genuinely unclear from the law itself.

::: {.disclaimer-box}
**Data currency:** This dashboard reflects a point-in-time research pass, completed August 2026. Laws change. Always verify current status with a qualified attorney or your state's workers' compensation board before relying on this resource for legal or financial decisions.
:::

## About ALERRT

This resource was developed by the [ALERRT Center](https://alerrt.org) at Texas State University. ALERRT conducts research on first responder training, health, and wellness, with a focus on improving outcomes for first responders and the communities they serve.
